chunks: Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them:

Regarding two men who have wealth between them, part of which is in their hands and part is absent from them, they divided the portion that was in their hands. Each one of them used cunning regarding his share. One of them took possession (of his share) and the other did not take possession. He said: 'What one of them took possession of, it is between them, and what was lost/absent, it is between them.'

key_terms.اقْتَسَمَا: They divided (specifically by measuring or allocating shares)

ai.seo_question: How is joint wealth divided when one partner takes possession and the other does not?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Hawalah* (debt transfer/assignment), this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the distribution of risk in partnership settlements. The Imam establishes that any portion of the joint wealth not yet physically seized by either partner remains a shared asset, ensuring that neither party bears the sole burden of loss for uncollected shares, thereby reinforcing the principle of equitable risk-sharing in commercial transactions.
